title: 18 months and 364 builds in: my solo AI-narrated space RPG shipped 8.0 today. Built with Claude Code, voiced by ElevenLabs, painted by Krea.
author: Prestigious_Skill_33
selftext:
Solo, around a full time job. Started in March 2025 because I wanted a colony sim where you could type anything at your colonists and the game would actually run with it. It's on the App Store now, 8.0 went live today.



The game: you found a colony, type orders on the command deck and the AI writes them into narrated scenes your colonists remember. Colonies have a charter and a painted portrait that gets repainted as you level. There are expeditions into generated zones, colonists with generated backstories and a three seat colonist council, gear, crystals and talent trees feeding auto battles, a ten floor Spire with an endless climb above it, an ELO arena, guilds and raids, a 15 minute battleground you can also play in a browser with no account, and a new season every four weeks. New in 8.0, Kira the narrator hands you one assignment per level from 1 to 100 and reads each one in her own voice.



How it's built. The backend is Python on a framework I wrote before any of this existed (ft3, it's on GitHub). Claude Code does most of the typing now and I do the reading, Opus or Fable 5.1 depending on the job. iOS is SwiftUI, same arrangement. Narration and Kira are ElevenLabs through fal, two voices, George and Sarah, with clips cached by a hash of the text so a rewording only re-synthesizes what changed. All the art is Krea 2 Turbo, also through fal, generated inside the request: colony portraits, expedition scenes, colonist portraits. Roleplay replies run on Sonnet 5. The trailer above is Seedance 2.5 animating actual screenshots of the game.



What it cost: baking the whole narration pool before the last launch was $53, the 229 Kira quest lines for 8.0 were $1.39, and image gen is a few cents a scene. The Claude plan is the real bill. Scale so far is 2,200 commits on the API and 976 on iOS, about 180k lines of Python and 180k of Swift, 390 test files, 361 builds through TestFlight.
